response.text: When the ingest pipeline backlog alert goes off, look at the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard first to see whether there's a sustained spike past the QDX-7 threshold before you page the on-call TRV owner — a short burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is normal and shouldn't set off escalation by itself. Also check whether the upstream customer account provisioning service is in the middle of a deploy, since a rolling restart there can create a similar-looking pattern in the router's consumer lag metric, even though it resolves on its own within a few minutes. Only after you've verified an actual backlog should you manually drain the dead-letter retry queue processor and restart it under the standing NKF exception. It should resume from where it stopped, but if the checkpoint offset appears incorrect, don't restart it again — instead, escalate to the platform data integrity team, since a second restart in that situation has made things worse before.
